newsitem.title: FINLAND: LIPPONEN SEES SWEDEN NOT JOINING EMU AT ONCE -STT.
newsitem.headline: LIPPONEN SEES SWEDEN NOT JOINING EMU AT ONCE -STT.

text.p: Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Tuesday he expected the Swedish government to decide against membership of European economic and monetary union (EMU) in the first wave, the Finnish news agency STT reported.

Speaking at briefing for Finnish political journalists, Lipponen said a Swedish no, or not yet, to EU would not come as a surprise, and he said he expected Sweden to join the single currency sooner or later, STT said.
The Swedish decision would not affect Finnish government policy on EMU, Lipponen added.
The coalition -- led by Lipponen's Social Democratic Party -- has repeatedly said Finland intends to join EMU in the first wave in 1999. Finland meets all convergence criteria.
A decision on EMU by Sweden's governing social democrats is expected later this afternoon.
